title: Vibhishana crosses
hookLine: Ravana's brother chooses the other side
carry: rama turns away no one who asks refuge
last: DHARMA OFFERS PEACE BEFORE THE FIGHT.

lines: THE ONLY ONE WHO SAYS IT.
cards: A family dinner where everyone agrees about something that's wrong, heads nodding around the table, and one person who can't nod along. The story rewinds a little, to a scene Valmiki puts before the bridge.
Inside Lanka, Ravana calls his council. Monkeys are gathering on the far shore. What should we do?
One after another, his generals and ministers say: we'll crush them, great king. Then his younger brother stands up. Vibhishana.
And he says the thing nobody in that golden room wants to hear.

teach.h: GIVE HER BACK, HE SAYS. TWICE.
teach.b: Give Sita back, Vibhishana tells his brother. Taking her was wrong, and it will destroy Lanka. Make peace with Rama.
He says it once, carefully, then again. And Ravana explodes.
He calls his brother a traitor and a disgrace to the family, and in some tellings, including Tulsidas's, kicks him in front of the whole court. So Vibhishana makes a choice people still argue about.
He rises into the air with four companions, crosses the sea, and hovers above Rama's camp. I'm Ravana's brother, he calls down. I've left everything.
I've come for refuge. The monkeys are sure it's a trick, and Sugriva says kill him. Rama says no.
In Valmiki's telling, Rama says it's his vow: anyone who comes to him even once asking for shelter, saying I am yours, he will protect, from anything. Even, he adds, if it were Ravana himself.
Then, before a single battle, on the beach, Rama has Vibhishana anointed as the future king of Lanka.

The tradition holds Vibhishana two ways: devotees revere him as one who chose dharma over family, and an old Hindi saying remembers him as the insider who brought Lanka down. But the line people treasure is Rama's.

It has a name: sharanagati, taking refuge. Many Hindus, especially in the Sri Vaishnava tradition of south India, hold that verse as God's own promise. Whoever turns to him, even once, is not turned away.
Look at who received it first. Not a loyal monkey. The enemy's brother, the one everyone said to kill.

how: Hindu tradition honors Vibhishana as a devotee of Rama and one of the long-lived ones of tradition. Rama's promise of refuge to him is recited as a verse of assurance, especially in the Sri Vaishnava tradition, where it is central to sharanagati (taking refuge in God); the Hindi proverb about 'the insider bringing down Lanka' shows the other way people remember him.

o: a demon general deserting in the middle of war
Ravana's brother sneaking over to spy on Rama
Ravana's brother leaving Lanka for Rama's side

games.q: who did what — tap the pairs.
p: told Ravana to give Sita back
promised refuge to all who ask

s: Vibhishana left without ever warning his brother
he told Ravana the truth in the council, more than once, before he left.
Rama had him crowned before the war began
on the beach, Rama had Vibhishana anointed as the future king of Lanka.
Rama made Vibhishana prove himself for weeks before taking him in
Rama took him in at once: anyone who comes even once asking for shelter, he protects.

games.q: you're Rama. Ravana's own brother is hovering over your camp asking for refuge, and your allies say it's a trap. what do you do?
o: hold him prisoner until the war ends.
games.why: Rama takes him in: anyone who comes to him even once asking for shelter, he says, he will protect, even Ravana himself.

practice: There's a short prayer many Hindus say: Shri Rama sharanam mama. Rama, you are my refuge. If you pray, say it slowly three times, and let it mean: I don't have to carry this alone.
If you don't pray, think of someone others have written off who might be knocking at your door, and what one small welcome would look like.

wordCard.voice: Vibhishana crosses. Ravana's younger brother, who told the truth twice, then asked Rama for refuge, and was taken in.

orig.note: Sanskrit: Vibhishana, Ravana's younger brother, who crossed over to Rama.

carryVoice: Your line: Rama turns away no one who asks refuge. Not even Ravana's brother. Sixty days now.
